bullets.text: Tens of thousands of migrants have crossed into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco, with Spain's Prime Minister blaming traffickers and other EU countries criticising Madrid over the incident. At least 57 people have died trying to reach the territory.

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the fastest growing in the virus's history, with the death toll rising to almost 1,500. Health workers are battling to slow the outbreak while a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain may be months away.

The Archbishop of Canterbury has pledged to support a £100m fund aimed at helping communities affected by enslavement, during a visit to Ghana. This controversial fund symbolises a Christian belief in repentance.
The tiger prawn season in Australia's far north has begun with a record low number of trawlers operating.
Ben Carroll has been appointed as the new premier of Victoria following the ousting of Jacinta Allan.
A 'well-connected Melbourne businessman' has been found guilty of rape, but his name remains protected due to exceptions to open justice in Victoria.
Boeing is working to regain trust and profitability after a challenging decade, marking a significant effort to rebuild its standing in the aviation industry.
Extenet Systems, an operator of miniature cell towers, is in default on its bonds due to missed interest payments and alleged cash management violations.
Oil prices remain highly volatile due to ongoing tensions in the Gulf, with the potential for prices to quickly return to triple digits.
